dedupe_keys.name: utilizing remote sensing to assess the implication of tall building performance on the resilience of urban centers

description: Utilizing Remote Sensing to Assess the Implication of Tall Building Performance on the Resilience of Urban Centers is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Henry Burton, University of California Los Angeles (ucla.edu). Tall buildings have become a staple of the central business district in cities such as Los Angeles, San Francisco and San Diego. They facilitate increased residential and commercial development, offering higher density occupancy compared to their low-rise counterparts on the same area of land. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-7fha-0w54. Keywords: Tall Building, Performance-Based Earthquake Engineering, Urban Resilience, Remote Sensing, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning. Published 2020-02-02. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
